meta.title: Germinal Multi Target Pipeline
meta.subtitle: Structures, escape measurements and sequence counts, to the antigens each campaign designs against

cards.title: How a target gets chosen
items: Each campaign designs against exactly two antigens: the parental one, and a challenge antigen that defeats the existing antibody
For EGFR the challenge is artificial — one composite antigen carrying all six resistance substitutions, which keeps the optimization at two targets instead of seven
For XFG the challenge is XFG-Next, built from the three substitutions where the evolutionary forecast and the published escape map agree

The escape evidence is one outside dataset: a pseudovirus deep mutational scan of BD55-1205 escape and ACE2 binding, measured in a KP.3.1.1 spike background (Dadonaite et al. 2025, Journal of Virology 99(11)). The six EGFR substitutions come from reported clinical resistance instead; no escape screen was run in this paper

cards.title: What the targets do not settle
items: Three variants were withheld from design entirely (BA.2.86, JN.1 and PG.3.1) and only tested afterwards; the composite antigen was also split back into single substitutions and tested one at a time
The escape map was measured in a KP.3.1.1 background, not XFG, and one forecast substitution behaved differently when moved across backgrounds
Breadth beyond the two design targets is measured, not designed: withheld variants were only ever tested afterwards
Designing against both targets did not guarantee activity against each substitution on its own
